title: Pell County Mutual Aid — Two Deputies, Not Before 11:30

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - EOC Sheriff Desk, Training Room

caller.name: Sgt. Halvorsen
caller.label: Pell County Sheriff's Office — Duty Sergeant, Dispatch

callee.name: Sheriff Dale Rademacher
callee.label: Calder County Sheriff — Checkpoint Commander, EOC

transcript.speaker: Pell County Sergeant
transcript.text: Sheriff, Sergeant Halvorsen in Pell. We got your mutual aid page about the checkpoints.

transcript.speaker: Pell County Sergeant
transcript.text: Here's what I've got. I can send you two deputies with marked units. But they can't be in Calder before 11:30. They're finishing a court transport and I can't pull them off it.

transcript.speaker: Pell County Sergeant
transcript.text: I called Ritter for you, too. They say nobody until tomorrow's day shift. Their fall harvest traffic detail took everyone they have.

transcript.speaker: Pell County Sergeant
transcript.text: One more thing, and I want to be straight with you. My guys have never run an ag checkpoint. Not once. Who briefs them on what a Board permit actually looks like? Where's the wash station, the C and D setup? Do they need PPE, and who's handing it out?

transcript.speaker: Pell County Sergeant
transcript.text: And tell me where you want them to report: your EOC in Larkin or straight to a road. I have to page them back by 09:30 with a location and a name to ask for.

transcript.speaker: Pell County Sergeant
transcript.text: So, two deputies at 11:30. Do you want them or not?

voiceStyles.Pell County Sergeant: Man in his 50s, calm, practical small-county sergeant; talks fast because he has a dispatch board to run. Radio traffic murmurs faintly behind him.
voiceStyles.Calder County Sheriff: Man in his 50s, clipped, distracted; busy EOC room behind him.

instructorNote: Friction inject: the fourth primary checkpoint (Annex K hour 0–3) will miss 10:50 by about 40 minutes, and Ritter can't help today. Watch for SHF to accept Pell's two deputies, assign them to a site and line up a briefing (only a valid Board permit plus C&D lets a vehicle through, and the permit desk decides, not the deputy), and to tell EMD about the slip. Then see whether EMD reports it to the state EOC and starts weighing a National Guard request through the state EOC instead of acting as a county alone.
